processes.name: ABRICATE_RUN

meta.description: Screen assemblies for antimicrobial resistance against multiple databases

tools.name: abricate
tools.description: Mass screening of contigs for antibiotic resistance genes

input.name: databasedir
input.description: Optional location of local copy of database files, possibly with custom databases set up with `abricate --setupdb`

processes.script_excerpt:
def args    = task.ext.args   ?: ''
def prefix  = task.ext.prefix ?: "${meta.id}"
def datadir = databasedir ? "--datadir ${databasedir}" : ''
"""
## Symlink when necessary to rename the file to allow specifying the prefix variable inside report
## As the variable is what is used as the sample ID in the report file
if [[ "${assembly}" != "${prefix}.fasta" ]]; then
    ln -s ${assembly} ${prefix}.fasta
fi

abricate \\
    ${prefix}.fasta \\
    ${args} \\
    ${datadir} \\
    --threads ${task.cpus} \\
    > ${prefix}.txt

cat <<-END_VERSIONS > versions.yml
"${task.process}":
    abricate: \$(echo \$(abricate --version 2>&1) | sed 's/^.*abricate //' )
END_VERSIONS
"""
processes.script_summary: Screens nucleotide sequences against a ResFinder/VFDB/PlasmidFinder CAROdb-style database with abricate --acc --quiet, emitting a TSV hit table plus a versions record.

publish_dir_matches.expression: [ path: { "${params.outdir}/arg/abricate/${meta.id}" }, mode: params.publish_dir_mode, saveAs: { filename -> filename.equals('versions.yml') ? null : filename }, ]

processes.name: AMPCOMBI2_CLUSTER

meta.description: A submodule that clusters the merged AMP hits generated from ampcombi2/parsetables and ampcombi2/complete using MMseqs2 cluster.

tools.name: ampcombi2/cluster
tools.description: A tool for clustering all AMP hits found across many samples and supporting many AMP prediction tools.

input.name: summary_file
input.description: A file corresponding to the Ampcombi_summary.tsv that is generated by running 'ampcombi complete'. It is a file containing all the merged AMP results from all samples and all tools.

processes.script_excerpt:
def args = task.ext.args ?: ''
"""
ampcombi cluster \\
    --ampcombi_summary ${summary_file} \\
    ${args} \\
    --threads ${task.cpus}
"""
processes.script_summary: Runs AMPCombi cluster on concatenated AMP screening hit tables to dereplicate and cluster predicted antimicrobial peptides across tools.

publish_dir_matches.expression: [ path: { "${params.outdir}/reports/ampcombi2" }, mode: params.publish_dir_mode, saveAs: { filename -> if (filename.equals('versions.yml')) { return filename } else { return !params.run_taxa_classification ? filename : null } }, ]

processes.name: AMPCOMBI2_COMPLETE

meta.description: A submodule that merges all output summary tables from ampcombi/parsetables in one summary file.

tools.name: ampcombi2/complete
tools.description: This merges the per sample AMPcombi summaries generated by running 'ampcombi2/parsetables'.

input.name: summaries
input.description: The path to the list of files corresponding to each sample as generated by ampcombi2/parsetables.

processes.script_excerpt:
def args = task.ext.args ?: ''
"""
ampcombi complete \\
    --summaries_files '${summaries.collect{file_path -> "$file_path"}.join("' '")}' \\
    ${args}

reference_rebuilds[] (11 rules) was detected over subworkflows/local/*.nf, subworkflows/nf-core/*/main.nf and workflows/*.nf by pairing an if/else-if/else branch that consumes params.X directly with a sibling branch that invokes a builder process instead. funcscan uses both the positive form (if (params.X_db) { fromPath } else { BUILDER() }) and the inverted form (if (!params.X_db) { BUILDER() } else { use }), neither of which the published detector matches for this shape (galaxyproject/foundry#229, #349), so all 11 rules come from this run's own pass. Three things the pairing needed that a name-shaped detector cannot see: include aliases (arg.nf calls the UNTAR module UNTAR_CARD, so a canonical-name-only process set misses the CARD download entirely), multi-step rebuilds (arg_rgi_db is fetched by UNTAR_CARD and then processed by RGI_CARDANNOTATION; the rule names the producer and records the second step in evidence[]), and a builder whose source is a hard-coded URL rather than a param (https://card.mcmaster.ca/latest/data, recorded in evidence[]). Where the rebuild branch is a bare `else`, `guard` is the derived negation of the preceding branch conditions rather than verbatim source text, and says so. The enclosing stage guard (for example !params.bgc_skip_antismash) is carried in evidence[] rather than folded into `guard`. Every asset_param was asserted to exist in params[] before emission.

workflow{} in main.nf is anonymous; it is recorded as subworkflows[] row RUN_MAIN_WORKFLOW_GLUE (kind: utility) because the summary schema has no slot for an unnamed workflow. FUNCSCAN is the primary named workflow and lives in workflow{}, not subworkflows[], so in_subworkflows[] never cites FUNCSCAN - processes reached only from FUNCSCAN list the subworkflows that wrap them (ANNOTATION/AMP/ARG/BGC/CAZYME/TAXA_CLASS/PROTEIN_ANNOTATION) or [].

params[].default is taken from the params { } block of nextflow.config, not from nextflow_schema.json: the schema carries a default for only 91 of the 220 params and for 3 of the 102 booleans, while nextflow.config assigns every param explicitly, so the schema alone would report a null default for 129 params that do have one. Nextflow resolves runtime param values from config, not from the schema, so config wins where the two differ; 0 such conflicts were found. Defaults left null are genuinely unset (config assigns null).
